o: For query (f, sec) we need a substring whose value v satisfies v = f XOR sec. Since f, sec <= 1e9 < 2^30, v < 2^30, so any matching substring has length at most 30 (and cannot have leading zeros unless it is exactly "0"). Strategy: precompute, for every starting index, all substring values of length up to 30, recording for each value the best (shortest, then leftmost) occurrence. Each query is then an O(1) hash lookup of f^sec. With |s| = 1e4 this is about 3e5 candidate values.
k: v = first ^ second is fully determined per query, so invert the problem: index all short substrings by value.
Only substrings of length <= 30 matter because values fit in 30 bits; substrings starting with '0' are useless except "0" itself.
Scanning starts left-to-right and storing the first (shortest) hit yields minimum left automatically.

a.n: Approach 1: Hash Map of All Short Substrings
a.i: Precompute a map value -> [left,right], keeping the shortest and leftmost occurrence per value; answer queries by lookup of first^second.
s: For each i with s[i]=='1', extend rightward up to 30 chars building the running value; record unseen values.
Also map value 0 to every single '0' position (keep leftmost).
For each query, look up first^second; output [-1,-1] if absent.
a.t: O(30n + q) — building the map dominates

w: Key trap: substrings with leading zeros. Only "0" itself is a valid representation of 0; "00" or "01" are never shortest/correct answers. Also cap extension at 30 bits to bound work. Follow-up: huge s with small alphabet — a trie of binary substrings achieves the same asymptotics with less memory.
